newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on fund selling, CBOT slide.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on fund selling, CBOT slide.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower on lower CBOT soycomplex values and fund sales, traders said.
"We followed Chicago. The funds sold 500 nearby, there's commercial scale down buying and scale down Japanese buying," a trader said.
CBOT soybean and meal futures tumbled on news Brazil soybeans were being shipped to the U.S. and on a slowdown in the weekly soybean crush pace, traders there said.

May WCE futures crush profit margin fell to -12.35 Friday from -11.18 Thursday. One thousand Sep-Nov spread at $5 as RBC-DS sold to UGG, traders said. May-July spread at $4. Volume was 10,831 lots, or 216,620 tonnes, with 380 hedges lots.
Japan bought 4,000-5,000 tonnes canola overnight, sources said. XCan denied rumours it sold 18,000 tonnes new crop to Germany.
May fell $7.20 to $420.50 and July tumbled $7.40 to $423.60. May flax fell $3 to $354 on comercial sales, July fell $4 to $350.50. Volume was 700 lots with 50 hedge lots.
May western barley slipped $1 to $138.70 and July fell $1 to $137.80 on commercial and farmer selling. Volume totaled 1,300.
May feed wheat lost $1 to $166.20, July fell $1.20 to $163.50 on spillover pressure. Volume was 450 lots.
July oats fell the US$5 limit to US$121 in commercial trade. Volume 35 lots.
May feedpeas fell US$4 to US$213 with RBC-DS selling. Volume was 60 lots.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne, except feedpeas)
